idea: MineAssist-PdM Enterprise - predictive maintenance platform for mining trade associations

selected_gap.title: Mining-Specific Natural Language Vibration Diagnosis
selected_gap.pain: Maintenance teams struggle to translate complex vibration data and dashboards into actionable maintenance decisions, leading to delayed responses and reliance on scarce expert analysts.
selected_gap.why_now: Advances in NLP make it technically feasible to generate domain-specific, clear recommendations, while established mining vibration providers (e.g., Bently Nevada) still rely on rule-based outputs and pure-play AI startups (e.g., Augury) are just beginning to enter mining.
selected_gap.evidence_needed: Customer discovery with mining maintenance managers to quantify time lost interpreting data and gauge willingness to pay for explainable NLP outputs; competitive analysis of Augury's mining traction.
selected_gap.risk: Augury accelerates mining deployment with its strong NLP and funding; incumbents may add NLP features to existing dashboards.

vc_rubric_scores.rationale: Assumes team has combined mining maintenance and AI expertise; not proven but plausible given domain focus.
Global mining PdM TAM likely >$1B; growing due to digitalization and skills shortage; timing is right.
Mining-specific explainable AI creates defensibility; natural language output is differentiated from rule-based tools.
No pilots or customers yet; only gap analysis and concept; significant evidence required.
SaaS to associations with outcome-based pricing can yield high margins; LTV:CAC >3x achievable if distribution through associations.
Incumbents (Bently) have data and trust; Augury is AI-focused and entering mining; differentiation is narrow but defensible if mining-specific model works.
No financial projections provided; assume moderate burn for prototype; 18+ months runway not confirmed.
Main risk: incumbents add NLP features; mining conservative adoption; realistic failure mode is failure to get association buy-in.

decision: Proceed with focused customer discovery and prototype development; do not scale until pilot validation.
next_experiments: Conduct 20 interviews with mining maintenance managers to quantify time lost interpreting vibration data and price sensitivity.
Build a prototype using public dataset (CWRU) that generates natural language repair instructions; test with 5 technicians.
Approach 3 mining trade associations (e.g., National Mining Association, ICMM) to gauge interest in benchmarking and insurance negotiation features.
kill_criteria: No association interest or pilot commitment within 3 months.
Incumbents (Bently Nevada or Augury) launch a competing NLP feature with mining traction within 6 months.
Customer discovery reveals that technicians prefer existing workflow over NLP recommendations (e.g., do-nothing or manual interpretation).
_iteration_one_liner: We equip mining trade associations with a white-label predictive maintenance platform that converts vibration anomalies into plain-language repair steps, cutting downtime and upskilling workers industry-wide.
